item.title: Discrepancies highlighted in new forestry scheme
item.description: A new reconstitution scheme looks set to grant local owners to replant damaged areas. Minister for Forestry, Michael Healy-Rae has confirmed that up to €55m will be available to private forestry owners affected by Storms Darragh and Éowyn through the financial aid scheme. While under new setback rules, any existing unplanted setback of up to 60 metres from nearby dwellings-including houses located across a public road-must remain unplanted at the reforestation stage. item.description: Local Fianna Fáil members can expect a full review into the party's presidential election campaign before Christmas. item.title: No injuries reported in Strokestown house fire
item.description: There were no injuries following a house fire in the Strokestown area last night. Fire services from Elphin and Strokestown responded to the incident shortly after 10 o'clock. Advertisement While no injuries were reported it's believed the property on the outskirts of the town suffered some smoke damage. Advertisement No cause has yet been established.

item.title: Former minister remembered for courage during the Troubles at funeral Mass
item.description: Athlone's Paddy Cooney has been remembered for his great courage as justice minister during the Troubles at his funeral Mass. A local bishop said he did the state great service, before his death at the age of 94. Mr Cooney was justice minister during the Troubles in the 1970s and served in several other ministries in the 80s. Advertisement His funeral Mass was held this morning in St Mary's Church in Athlone. item.title: Engaged man died from 'toxic' amount of alcohol and drugs, Carrick inquest hears
item.description: A 28-year-old man, who was engaged to be married, died after taking a toxic amount of alcohol and drugs in Carrick-on-Shannon last year. A sergeant said he was the victim of the many challenges facing society today. This inquest took place at the coroner's court in Carrick into the death of a man just outside the town last year. Advertisement It heard he had been in a friend's house nearby from around 8pm to 9.30pm, when they talked about lots of things, including setting up a business together.

item.title: New national drugs strategy to target rural towns and villages
item.description: Minister of State Jennifer Murnane O'Connor says the new national drugs strategy will feature a renewed focus on rural towns and villages. She was speaking during a visit to Roscommon today where she met with local groups including the North West Regional Drugs Task Force. In July, Roscommon coroner Brian O'Connor raised concern about the number of drugs and alcohol-related inquests coming before him. item.title: Judge dismisses Castlerea prison officer’s data breach claim
item.description: A Castlerea prison officer who sought compensation for alleged non-material damage arising from a data breach has had his claim dismissed, after a judge found no evidence that the incident caused harm beyond "mere upset." Judge Fergus ruled that while Mark Walsh, experienced "some discomfort and embarrassment" in the workplace after documentation concerning him was improperly disclosed, the legal threshold required to award damages had not been met. item.title: Local Senator demands end-to-end scheme to fix houses built with defective blocks
item.description: A local Senator has called for an end-to-end scheme to remediate houses that have been damaged by the use of defective concrete blocks. Sligo–Leitrim Senator Nessa Cosgrove told the Seanad that poorly built homes are leaving North-West families living in fear. item.title: Former Leitrim holiday resort back up for sale
item.description: A once-bustling holiday complex in county Leitrim has returned to the market. The former Breffni Holiday Village, located in Dromahair has a guide price of €1.2 million. It has re-entered the market due to a cancellation.
